'''Mojżesz David Kirszbraun''' (1903–1942)<ref>''[https://www.ushmm.org/online/hsv/person_view.php?PersonId=6965617 Mojżesz Kirszbraun]'', Holocaust Survivors and Victims Database.</ref> was a Polish mathematician, mostly known for the [[Kirszbraun theorem]] on extensions of Lipschitz maps. This theorem appears in his master's thesis, defended in Warsaw in 1930.

Kirszbraun finished school<!--Gimnazjum Kreczmara, Warsaw--> in 1922. Together with his classmate [[Adolf Lindenbaum]], he continued his studies in [[Warsaw University]]. Later, he worked as an actuary in an insurance company<!-- "Przyszłość"-->.
He died in a ghetto in 1942.
